accuracy.evidence: Matched to NC Y2 Measurement: compare and order lengths, mass, volume/capacity and record the results using >, < and =. Every value checked by hand: ribbon from 4 to 16 = 12 cm, 45 cm > 32 cm, 150 g < 400 g, 500 ml = 500 ml, 9 cm < 15 cm < 22 cm, 1 m = 100 cm > 90 cm, pencil from 2 to 10 = 8 cm < 10 cm, 60 cm > 6 cm, 3 kg < 5 kg. The kitchen scale dial is linear from 0 to 500 g and the measuring jug is marked every 100 ml.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented Y2 measuring slips: reading the end mark when the object does not start at 0 (ribbon at 4, pencil at 2, tag zero), bigger means heavier (big box vs small tin, tag size), taller holds more (tall vs wide jug, tag tall), comparing numbers across units (90 cm vs 1 m, tag unit), same digit taken as same size (60 cm vs 6 cm, tag digit) and the sign turned the wrong way (tag flip).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagcmpm is a measure-then-record lab: a draggable ribbon on a cm ruler, a dial kitchen scale, a measuring jug that two different-shaped jugs pour into, staggered strings ordered by their cm values and a 1 m vs 90 cm conversion, all ending in a dragged <, = or > symbol. flagord1k and flagcmp2d compare bare numbers; flaglenht, flagmass and flagcups use non-standard units; flagunits chooses units. Lab gate overlap under 30%.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner slides the ribbon and sees the reading change until it starts at 0, watches the needle show the small tin is heavier, sees both jugs fill the measuring jug to the same 500 ml line, finds that the red string reaches farthest yet is not longest, and has to press 'Change 1 m to cm' before the comparison passes; the step text confirms each rule afterwards.

predictions.evidence: Six predictions, each with a tempting wrong option that the lab disproves: '16 cm' for the ribbon, '<' for 45 cm _ 32 cm, 'the big box' as heavier, 'the tall jug' as holding more, 'red, it reaches farthest' as longest and '90 cm, 90 is more than 1'.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Seven challenge pairs; every wrong symbol has a tag (flip, same, size, tall, unit, digit, zero) with its own message naming that slip, e.g. 'It did not start at 0. From 2 to 10 is only 8 cm, so it is less than 10 cm.'

readability.evidence: Kid text uses short sentences and Year 2 terms (measure, ruler, cm, g, ml, more, less, same) and passes the family kid readability target in validate_lessons; adult text names the programme of study, explains fair comparison and lists four common mistakes.

no_filler.evidence: Content gate is clean. Kid paragraphs each add one rule (measure both from 0, record with a sign, measure instead of judging by looks, same units then order) and each lab step practises one of them.

mobile.evidence: Checked on iPhone 13 screenshots in light and dark: the 1.2 tall canvas keeps ruler labels at 11 px with labels every 5, 10 or 20 cm so they never collide, the symbol tiles are about 57 x 60 px, the parcel and jug cards are about 150 px wide, and the young-mode DOM buttons are 56 px; nothing is clipped at 390 px.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a button twin (Slide left/right, Weigh the box/tin, Pour the tall/wide jug, Change 1 m to cm, <, =, > buttons, Pick then Put shortest/middle/longest); the canvas aria-label is updated with every spoken result; walk.cjs axe WCAG 2.1 AA is clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone.

sources: Department for Education, National Curriculum in England: mathematics programmes of study, Year 2 measurement: compare and order lengths, mass, volume/capacity and record the results using >, < and =
Department for Education, Year 2 measurement: choose and use appropriate standard units to estimate and measure length/height in any direction (m/cm), mass (kg/g) and capacity (litres/ml)
NCETM Year 2 measures guidance on common errors: not starting at zero on a ruler and judging mass or capacity by size or height
